text:
maria: Heads-up — saw a perf regression on the int8 path after yesterday's kernel selection change. +12% p99 on chat workloads in the canary. cc @aj @samir :thinking:

aj: ugh. do we have a flamegraph/profile link? is it latency per-token or end-to-end?

infra-bot: profiling snapshot uploaded: https://prof.redwood.internal/snapshots/1780123456 (flame + timeline)

samir: looked quickly — hotspot is in the int8 attention kernel when batch_size <= 4. perf cliff there. flame shows more kernel launch overhead + cache misses (KV accesses) compared to fp8 path. snippet: ```
# flame excerpt
int8_attention_kernel  42%  \nkernel_launch_overhead  8%\nkv_lookup_serial 12%\n```

maria: interesting — our kernel router switched priority to the new int8 kernels for small seq lengths; wasn't expecting that to regress small-batch latency. could batching heuristics be shrinking batches?

aj: yes — we tightened the continuous batching window from 15ms -> 8ms to improve tail latency for streaming. side-effect: fewer requests are coalesced, so int8 (which needs bigger batches to saturate) loses throughput.

samir: exactly. two levers: 1) kernel routing bias (prefer fp8/int8 depending on batch/seq) 2) adaptive batching window (grow when throughput drops). simple heuristic: if observed mean batch_size < 6 for 2s, increment window by +5ms up to 25ms.

docsguy: for SDK/docs: we need to expose knobs so users can pick presets. propose new params on the client: `quant_preset` (safe|balanced|speed), `calibration_mode` (auto|manual|none), `degradation_threshold` (float 0-1), and `safety_fallback=true|false`. Example: ```js
redwood.generate({
  model: "rwt-3b-quant",
  quant_preset: "balanced",
  calibration_mode: "auto",
  safety_fallback: true,
  degradation_threshold: 0.02
})
```

maria: those look good. semantics: `quant_preset=safe` should avoid int8/fp4 for short-chat workloads and prefer fp8/fp16; `speed` should bias toward fastest kernels even if slightly higher error. `balanced` is default.

vikas: also add runtime-exposed telemetry: `kernel_selected`, `observed_batch_size`, `kv_cache_reuse_ratio`, `calibration_quality_delta` so Console can trigger alerts.

aj: +1. telemetry enables automated rollouts: canary -> monitor `nll_regression > 0.01` or `p99_latency_up > 5%` then rollback.

samir: about KV cache: we see more serialized KV lookups when batches are tiny. two suggestions: 1) batch KV lookups across inflight requests before calling kernel; 2) coalesce identical prefixes into shared KV views. both reduce memory traffic.

docsguy: for docs explainers, short bullets: - what each preset does - calibration implications (time + sample prompts) - safety rails: autopin FP when `degradation_threshold` exceeded - how to trigger manual calibration and view calibration stats.

maria: calibration_mode details please: auto should run quick quant-calib with ~1000 random tokens from recent traffic; manual should accept a labeled prompt set and run longer. calibration outputs: `scale_map` + `per_layer_bias` and an estimated `quality_score`.

docsguy: will draft UX copy. question: what is a safe default for `degradation_threshold`? 0.02? 0.01?

samir: 0.02 seems reasonable as default; it's permissive enough for small noise but will avoid noticeable regressions. if customers opt-in to `speed`, default threshold can be 0.05.

vikas: action items: - add knobs to SDK params + JS/py examples (docsguy) - implement adaptive batching heuristic and kernel router bias (aj + samir) - telemetry events + Console alerts (vikas) - create canary config: 10% traffic on dedicated pools then 50% if stable (maria)

docsguy: draft preset table for docs: `safe` -> prefer fp8/fp16, calibration: auto, fallback: on; `balanced` -> default mix, calibration: auto, fallback: on; `speed` -> prefer int8/fp4, calibration: recommended, fallback: optional. will add examples and a short troubleshooting checklist.

maria: please add a small note in the Console rollout UI: "Quantization presets can change latency/quality. Watch NLL, embedding cosine drift, and p99 latency."

aj: quick internal note — PR for adaptive batching heuristic: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/4021 (WIP). kernel router patch in 4022. samir will add int8 launch coalescing in 4023.

infra-bot: new canary created: dedicated-pool-quant-canary-20260316, traffic=10%

docsguy: will upload a one-page explainer and sample config to the docs repo after PRs land. also adding a short migration guide for customers using older quant knobs.

maria: assign owners and deadlines? prefer small incremental rollouts: adaptive batching + router bias in stage by EOW, SDK params + docs text next week, canary watch for 72h. owners: aj/samir (runtime), docsguy (docs), vikas (telemetry/alerts).

vikas: noted. I'll add alert rules: p99_latency_up > 7% OR nll_regression > 0.015 for 5m -> paging.

samir: one more perf tip: for sequence length distribution with heavy short-chat tail, prioritize kernel that benefits latency at batch<=4 even if throughput dips slightly. we can make that a config on the router `latency_first_threshold=4`.

maria: thanks all. we'll reconvene after 24h of canary metrics. :rocket:
